fix: In 'Corolla …; tube …, N mm long', the measurement after 'tube' belongs to the corolla tube, not the whole corolla. A sub-part named after a semicolon should take the measurement.
reason: The 1.2–2 mm length is the length of the tube. The limb is described separately, and the whole corolla is longer than 2 mm.

fix: Here 'flowering' means flowering stems (stems that bear flowers), not the flowering stage. The stage slot does no harm, but the better reading is a kind of stem.
reason: The flowering stems are described as densely sericeous, so 'stem sericeous' is true of the stems described.
The monocarps (fruitlets) are dark red at maturity. Fruit with the 'mature' context matches what the flora says.
In 'ovate to lanceolate', lanceolate is one end of the range for the sepals.

target: arrangement in one row (uniseriate) on each side of the pinna midrib
fix: In 'in N row(s)', N counts rows, not the part. Read it as an arrangement (in one row, uniseriate), not as the number of the part.
reason: The flora does not say there is one sorus on each side. It says the sori are in one row, and that they are more numerous above the midrib.

fix: A section heading such as 'Female flowers:' / 'Fleurs pistillées' should fill the whole/state slot for all the statements under it.
reason: The 2–4 tepals are said of the pistillate flowers only, but the annotation has no female-flower context.
The leaflets are obovate or oblong.

fix: 'outside' and 'within' should set the place on the part (the outer or inner surface), as 'beneath' and 'above' already do.
reason: Only the outer side of the corolla is glabrous. The lobes are pilose within, so 'corolla glabrous' without the place is false.
The leaflets are pilose beneath. The lower (abaxial) epidermis of the leaf is an acceptable bearer.
The flora says 'Sepals green'.

fix: 'peduncle' was mapped to pedicel. Check the lexicon: peduncle is PO_0009053.
reason: The 1–1.5 cm length is the length of the peduncle of the umbel, not of a pedicel.

fix: Perianth symbols '♂' and '♀' (and 'périgone ♀') should fill the whole/state slot.
reason: The lanceolate segments belong to the female perianth. The male perianth segments are ovate, so 'tepal lanceolate' without the female context is false.

fix: The positions 'dorsal' and 'lateral' sepal should fill the position slot. Also, a hyphenated shape such as 'ovate-oblong' should not be reduced to its last word alone.
reason: Only the dorsal sepal is ovate-oblong. The lateral sepals are narrowly elliptic or ovate.
The flora says 'stigmates 3'.
The flora says the leaflets are not viscid.
'suborbicular' is correctly read as approximately orbicular.
The calyx is up to 11 mm long in the fruit stage, and the open lower bound is right.

fix: A colour synonym marked RELATED that crosses level-1 colours (here fuscous → red) should not be emitted as a value. In botany, 'fuscous' means dark greyish brown.
reason: Fuscous fern scales are dark brown, not red. The bearer (scales on the stipe read as a trichome) is acceptable.

fix: The subject of the comparison is the filament. It should not be raised to the stamen.
reason: The filaments equal the sepals. The whole stamen, with its anther, is longer.

fix: A heading such as 'Basal leaves:' / 'Cauline leaves:' should fill the whole/position slot for the sub-parts that follow it.
reason: The 3–8 cm petiole belongs to the basal leaves only. The cauline leaves are described separately.
'Leaves numerous' means the leaves are present and many.

fix: A stage phrase that follows the alternatives ('X or Y when young, becoming Z') should fill the stage slot for all the alternatives.
reason: The branchlets are purple or dull brown only when young. Later they become grayish brown.

fix: 'palmately cleft' could map to palmatifid (cut about halfway), the more specific class under palmately lobed.
reason: A palmately cleft leaf is palmately lobed, so the value is true, only less specific than it could be.
The petals are slightly shorter than the dorsal sepal.
The leaves are sessile or subsessile.

target: plant cell (PO_0009002) of the leaf lamina
fix: In 'cells of X quadrate …', the shape belongs to the cells. The bearer should be the cell, with X as its whole.
reason: The quadrate-to-hexagonal shape is the shape of the lamina cells, not of the leaf.
The leaf blade is puberulent on its upper (adaxial) side.

target: glabrous or sparsely pubescent (leaflets); 'pubescent hair' is not a value
fix: 'with a few hairs' means sparsely hairy. PATO_0001320 'pubescent hair' is a hair, not a hairiness value.
reason: The second alternative is 'a few white hairs' on the leaflets. The value given is not a pilosity value.
Ochreolae are the sheathing bracts of the inflorescence, and they are strigose.
The pedicels are glabrous or nearly so.
